newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark to issue 10-month treasury bills.
newsitem.headline: Denmark to issue 10-month treasury bills.

text.p: Denmark's central bank on Tuesday said that it would begin issuing 10-month treasury bills, instead of nine-month paper, at an auction of the 1998II series on June 27, with settlement on July 1.

The bank said in a statement that during the changeover period there would be eight auctions in each series instead of the usual seven, with issuance of the 10-month bills continuing until three months before maturity.

It said that sales of its six percent 1999I and four percent 2000I treasury notes, and the six percent 2002, five percent 2005, seven percent 2007 and seven percent 2024 government bonds would continue in the second half of 1997.

The bank added that as ordinary repayments on outstanding government securities were lower in 1997 than last year it intended to make repurchases of series falling due in 1998 during the second half of 1997, market conditions permitting.

At close of business on June 16 the central bank had sold 47.9 billion crowns worth of government securities. Latest government figures put the 1997 borrowing requirement at 62.0 billion. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
